background_notes.fact: For the supplied Fourier Sobolev norms, r<=s implies ||h||_(H^r)<=||h||_(H^s); ||partial_x h||_(H^r)<=||h||_(H^(r+1)). On smooth periodic functions, Dinv partial_x=P, S_t commutes with partial_x,Dinv,P, and ||Dinv h||_2<=||h||_2. B_t has zero mean. Thus the stages, C_n,Q_n,W_n,Y_n and Y_n' used here are mean zero. For smooth mean-zero h, N006 applied to partial_x h gives ||S_t h||_infinity<=C||h||_(H^1), uniformly in t.

background_notes.justification: The weight inequalities <k>^(2r)<=<k>^(2s), k^2<=<k>^2 and |k|^(-2)<=1 for k!=0 give the norm bounds by summing nonnegative Fourier terms. Diagonal multipliers commute and (ik)^(-1)(ik)=1 at nonzero modes, zero at zero. The derivative defining B kills its zero mode; the R2 definition kills its zero mode, so all displayed integral and linear combinations preserve zero mean. For mean-zero h, Dinv partial_x(S_t h)=S_t h; N006 bounds this by C||partial_x S_t h||_2<=C||h||_(H^1). These observations justify the weaker stage norms, the S003 L^infty estimate and the mean-zero premises in S005.

background_notes.fact: For a continuous path G into a Hilbert space on [a,b], its time integral obeys ||integral_a^t G(s)ds||<=integral_a^t||G(s)||ds<=(t-a) sup_[a,t]||G||. If G is continuous, the integral has derivative G. Bounded linear maps commute with these integrals. These facts apply on each smooth step to F_n,C_n,Q_n,Y_n and to Dinv Y_n.

Difference quotients of the integral converge to the integrand by continuity. On each step the smooth spatial inputs make the displayed B/J expressions continuous in every fixed Sobolev norm, so this reasoning applies.
